slides.title: You're not "tempted" by p*rn. [[You're bored. Fix your day.]]
slides.sub: Most Day 12 relapses aren't about desire at all.

slides.title: Boredom [[dressed up]]
slides.body: An empty evening, nothing planned, phone in hand. That "urge" is often just boredom looking for the easiest hit — p*rn.

slides.title: Your day is [[empty]]
slides.body: No training. No plans. No goals for tonight. If your day has nothing in it, p*rn will fill it.

slides.title: Stop blaming [[willpower]]
slides.body: You don't need more willpower. You need a fuller day. Busy people relapse less.

slides.title: Fill tonight [[now]]

carousels.name: Every hour on your phone in bed

slides.title: Every extra hour on your phone in bed [[raised the odds of insomnia by 59%.]]
slides.sub: And late-night scrolling is where most p*rn starts.

slides.title: Per [[hour]] in bed
slides.body: A Frontiers in Psychiatry study (2025) of ~40,000 students found each extra hour of screen use after going to bed was tied to 59% higher odds of insomnia symptoms. That's screens in general — not just p*rn.

slides.title: Bed + phone = [[p*rn risk]]
slides.body: Late night, alone, tired, phone in hand — the exact setup many people describe before p*rn. Worse sleep. Weaker brakes. More p*rn.

slides.title: The [[loop]]
slides.body: Bad sleep makes you tired and impulsive tomorrow — which makes p*rn harder to resist tomorrow night. Break it at the bed.

slides.title: The [[bed rule]]
items: Bed is for sleep — not scrolling, not p*rn.
Old-school alarm clock if you need one.

slides.sub: Screenshot it. Follow it. Finish strong.

slides.title: [[Lock]] the doors
slides.body: Block p*rn on every device. Delete the apps that lead you there. Phone out of the bedroom. Make relapse hard.

slides.title: Fill the [[gaps]]
slides.body: Mid-month boredom is real. Plan your evenings: training, people, one new skill. Empty evenings are where p*rn wins.

carousels.name: What p*rn cost you this year: a brutal audit

slides.title: What p*rn cost you this year. [[Add it up. Don't look away.]]
slides.sub: Most people never do this math.

slides.title: Your [[time]]
slides.body: 30 minutes of p*rn a day is about 182 hours a year. An hour a day is 365. That's weeks of your life — every year.

slides.title: Your [[sleep]]
slides.body: How many nights did p*rn keep you up past 1 AM? Count them. Then count the mornings you felt wrecked.

slides.title: Your [[people]]
slides.body: Plans you skipped. Calls you ignored. Partners you pushed away. P*rn rarely costs only you.

slides.title: Finish the [[audit]]
items: Then decide: is p*rn worth another year?
